subject: Sequencing the multi-team walkthrough after site incident
messages:
From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@clearstream.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@clearstream.com>; Linda Park <linda.park@clearstream.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Scheduling the hands-on walkthrough

Hi Mina —

Quick update from our side: our primary network team is still waiting on DC vendor Ops to restore console access after yesterday's regional site incident. Without that, our infra engineer can't run the live environment checks or join the hands-on portion of the demo. Procurement is also hitting a brief pause while they validate the vendor-impact statement.

We really want to keep momentum, but holding the full technical session today won't be productive. Can we push the interactive portion to next week? If you have an exec-level product overview we could still run for the wider stakeholder group (PMs/VPs) that doesn't require infra access, that would be helpful.

Appreciate recommendations on how to split this so we don't lose traction.

Thanks,
Tom
Customer Success Lead — ClearStream

Attachments referenced: none
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sequencing the multi-team walkthrough after site incident

Tom — thanks for the heads up and sorry to hear about the vendor-side outage. Totally agree we should avoid scheduling a live, hands-on session if your engineer can't access the environment.

Suggested approach to keep momentum:
- Run an executive-level overview (30–40 mins) for PMs/VPs that covers value, ROI examples, integration patterns — no infra access needed.
- SE (Marissa) will record a 20–25 min deep-dive demo showing the exact steps we planned; record will be available for your infra and security teams to review asynchronously.
- Once your vendor restores console access, we schedule a 90-min hands-on lab with your infra engineer and our SE to validate end-to-end.

Proposed tentative windows:
- Exec overview: Wed 2027-04-07 10:00–10:40 PT OR Thu 2027-04-08 13:00–13:40 PT
- Hands-on lab: to be scheduled post-restoration (we can tentatively hold Thu 2027-04-15 09:00–10:30 PT)

I attached our draft agenda and a quick SOC2 snapshot Marissa mentioned to show baseline controls while you work through procurement. If you prefer, we can also do a short live Q&A with our product team during the exec overview.

If those windows look reasonable, I'll send calendar invites and the recording plan.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks Mina — quick note from the SE side: I'm on travel Tue–Thu of next week (out of region) but I can record the deep-dive demo tomorrow afternoon (2027-04-02) and share the MP4+step-by-step notes. I can also join the exec overview remotely if we schedule it in the Wed 10:00 PT window, otherwise I'll dial in from a different timezone but still can participate.

On the security/ procurement ask: attaching the SOC2 snapshot we maintain for prospective customers; it often helps procurement and infosec triage the initial questions while they run their vendor checks. If ClearStream needs additional artifacts (pen test, encryption keys flow), we can coordinate through Aditya who handles compliance packs.

I'll produce:
- 22-min recorded SE demo (screen + narration)
- 2-page runbook showing the exact console checks we will do during the hands-on lab

Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Sequencing the multi-team walkthrough after site incident

Mina/Marissa — this plan looks good and should help keep stakeholders engaged. A couple of notes from procurement/security:
- Procurement is fine with the exec overview and recording for evaluation; they will not approve any hands-on keys until the vendor provides a formal incident impact notice.
- Our SSO provider is also impacted in the same incident, so live SSO-based signons won't work until access is restored. That means even if we wanted to do a limited live lab, we'd be forced to use temporary service accounts (procurement won't sign off on that).

Request: please proceed with the Wed 2027-04-07 10:00 PT exec overview and share the recording and runbook as soon as they're available. We'll plan the hands-on lab once we have the vendor update.

I'll loop vendor Ops (status@dc-ops.vendor.com) into this string for transparency.

Thanks,
Tom

Perfect — thanks for confirming Tom. Action items and next steps from Redwood:

1) Exec overview (hosted): Wed 2027-04-07 10:00–10:40 PT — invite will be sent to your stakeholder list. This will be a product/business-focused session and include a 10-min live Q&A.
2) SE deliverables: Marissa will share the recorded 22-min deep-dive and the 2-page runbook by tomorrow EOD (2027-04-04).
3) Hands-on lab: On hold until vendor confirms console access. We have a tentative hold for Thu 2027-04-15 09:00–10:30 PT; we'll convert to a firm invite once vendor provides green light.
4) Compliance artifacts: Aditya will be your contact for any additional evidence procurement requests (pen test, encryption flow diagram).

I attached the final draft agenda and included a one-click calendar propose link so folks can accept quickly. If anyone prefers a recorded-only path (no live Q&A), let me know — we can make the exec overview 25-min recorded and skip Q&A.

Thanks everyone — appreciate the transparency from VendorOps. We'll look to re-enable the hands-on as soon as the console is back.

Best,
Mina Haddad
